title: Toward an Integrative Model of Layoff Effects: A Strategic Human Capital Resources Framework
abstract: Despite decades of research yielding rich theoretical insights and empirical evidence, the layoff literature remains fragmented. It lacks an overarching framework integrating findings across levels of analysis (e.g., organizational, group, and individual), stakeholder groups (e.g., layoff decision‐makers, executioners, survivors, and displaced employees), and outcomes from proximal processes to distal performance consequences. This fragmentation impedes understanding of how layoff effects unfold and why they vary across individuals and organizations. We review and synthesize layoff research and integrate insights from recent advancements in the strategic human capital resources literature. Our framework explains how layoffs first trigger an outflow of human capital and then reshape the quality, complementarity, and deployment of remaining human capital resources, while shaping the social‐psychological reactions of stakeholder groups. We further identify layoff characteristics as contingencies that determine whether layoffs produce negative or positive shifts in strategic human capital resources states, shape stakeholder reactions, and condition whether individual outcomes aggregate

title: Green Human Resource Management: Sustainability and the Employment Relationship
abstract: This chapter examines the opportunities and tensions involved in embedding green human resource management (HRM) in diverse organizational contexts. It highlights how cultural and institutional conditions shape the possibilities and limits of green HRM practices. The chapter first considers the role of HR professionals in leading corporate sustainability, emphasizing their strategic and operational influence on workforce engagement with ecological goals. It then reviews core green HRM practices through the ability-motivation-opportunity (AMO) framework. Drawing on pluralist perspectives, it shows how green HRM bundles are shaped by power, trust, and employee voice across the employee life cycle. The chapter argues that green HRM is embedded in the contested employment relationship and that its effectiveness depends on fairness, employee involvement, and commitment to the common good. Environmental sustainability in the workplace thus becomes a negotiated terrain, where future research and practice should explore how HR can foster more just and sustainable organizational transformations.

title: The Rise of Multi-Agent AI in Strategic Human Resource Management: Exploring How Collaborative AI Agents Transform Talent Management, Workforce Coordination, and HR Decision Authority
venue: Journal of Business Insight and Innovation
abstract: This study examined how professionals in Pakistan understood the role of collaborative artificial intelligence (AI) agents in talent management, workforce coordination and HR decision authority. Guided by Socio-Technical Systems Theory and Organizational Information Processing Theory, the study used reflexive thematic analysis to interpret 20 online interviews with HR, operations and technology professionals. Six themes captured participants’ accounts of recruitment, career development, workforce planning, decision authority, procedural fairness and organizational readiness. Participants located a critical point of recruiter oversight at initial screening, when historical hiring preferences could exclude qualified applicants before human review. In development and scheduling, they identified employee aspirations, skills and personal circumstances as information that could change an otherwise plausible recommendation. They assigned responsibility for pay adjustments to compensation committees and staffing reductions to executives. Across functions, participants connected fairness with understandable reasons and access to a reviewer empowered to correct an outcome. The findings show

title: Data Science Job Profiles Classifiers Using Machine Learning
venue: Concurrency and Computation Practice and Experience
abstract: This research examines the power of various professional competencies and industry characteristics within the Data Science job market to classify profiles in Barcelona and Madrid. We utilized human resource classification criteria and Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Decision Trees, XGBoost, and CatBoost as classification algorithms to identify key variables that drive model interpretability and performance. These variables include education, experience, personal attributes such as adaptability and continuous learning, English level, specific insights, teamwork, and external stakeholders' interactions. Our analysis reveals that soft skills, industry experience, and educational background—particularly English proficiency—are the primary determinants of job market classification, guiding stakeholders in talent development and optimizing recruitment strategy. This study focuses on the variables essential to the classification models, thereby contributing to a more sophisticated understanding of job market dynamics. Specifically, we highlight the synergy between professional skills and industry context as the primary driver of market identity in Barcelona and Madrid. This synergy is cr

title: On-Demand Labour, Counterdata, and Worker Agency: Building Data Literacies in the Platform Economy
abstract: This chapter examines how platform workers develop new relationships with data, both to negotiate platform working conditions and to challenge algorithmic management. The chapter examines four data-driven projects (Turkopticon, Fairwork, Worker Info Exchange, and the Workers Observatory). It argues that each project cultivates a distinct but related form of data fluency. Such fluency is not an individual technical competence but a collective sociopolitical practice through which workers actively produce knowledge and evidence of platform working conditions and platform-based harms. While none of these projects can fully erase the fundamental asymmetries of platform labour, they do demonstrate that algorithmic systems are contested spaces, and that the strategic mobilisation of data fluency can meaningfully redistribute informational power.

title: When Data Scientists Meet Domain Experts: Artificial Intelligence, Epistemic Conflict, and Knowledge Transformation
abstract: Predictive artificial intelligence (AI) models developed by data scientists promise to transform organizational knowledge, yet in practice, the predictions remain inscrutable to domain experts. Existing explanations situate the problems in the opacity of the AI tools, failed adoption, or jurisdictional conflict but offer limited insight into how to make the knowledge accessible. Here, we show how the problem emerges from the competing epistemic stances of data scientists and domain experts, which create conflict over how to produce and evaluate knowledge. We then ask how data scientists and domain experts address that conflict so that their work with AI satisfies each group’s standards for producing and evaluating knowledge. Drawing on an 18-month inductive study of three large Indian banks, we show that the data scientists produce new knowledge, but domain experts hold the power to decide whether it is deployed. Our findings distinguish between epistemic and jurisdictional conflict. We show that data scientists first try to address the epistemic conflict directly through assimilative practices that follow one epistemic stance or the other. When these practices fail to transform kn

title: Sample Range as Subjective Variability and Implications for Experience-Based Decision Making
abstract: Variance and standard deviation are common metrics of statistical variability in the management and decision-making literature. In everyday contexts, however, information about sample range prevails. Range is arguably easier to comprehend and compute than variance, yet it often yields equivalent judgments about variability. Hence, we reason that decision makers often rely on range to judge variability. We test this hypothesis across four behavioral experiments (total n = 1,093). When comparing the variability of two number sets, decision makers predominantly based their judgments on sample range rather than sample variance when the two metrics disagree (experiment 1). Sample range tends to increase with sample size, whereas sample variance does not. Consistent with the range as variability hypothesis, decision makers perceived distributions as more variable after observing larger samples (experiment 2). This perceived variability, in turn, influenced risky decisions, as larger sample sizes led to decreased valuations of uncertain rewards for risk-averse decision makers (experiment 3). In further support of the hypothesis, when asked to mentally simulate new samples from a previousl

title: Rhythm and blues in hybrid work: Distinct working from home configurations and related HR policy demands
venue: German Journal of Human Resource Management Zeitschrift für Personalforschung
abstract: Working from home (WFH) research typically presents employees’ preferences and companies’ policies for offsite work in an aggregate manner but neglects differences between employees’ rationales in the light of how digital technology has formed their performative interaction in teams. In this paper we argue that the shortcoming results from underestimating the digital artifact as merely a passive job resource. Thus, we explore WFH preferences as contextualized construct reflecting individual, team, and technological characteristics of digital work also in their interrelatedness. Our theoretical framework adopts a sociomaterial perspective that integrates human-centric and team-centric approaches and guides the identification of distinct WFH configurations. The empirical basis consists of two cross-sectional surveys conducted in 2023 ( n = 296) and 2025 ( n = 290) among German-speaking respondents with WFH options. Using exploratory and confirmatory latent profile analyses to substantiate our configurational approach, we identify three different and robust profiles: (1) a Life Balance Profile emphasizing individual interests for offsite work while expecting HR policies supporting ind

title: Legal Governance of Digital Platform Practices: Reconciling Gig Economy Models With the Right to Decent Work
abstract: This chapter examines the legal governance of digital labor platforms, analyzing the tension between algorithmic management practices and the International Labour Organization's Decent Work Agenda. Through a comparative jurisprudential lens examining developments across the EU, UK, and US, including the UK Supreme Court's Uber v. Aslam ruling, Spain's Ley Rider, and the EU Platform Work Directive, this chapter evaluates the limitations of reactive judicial remedies and third-category labor classifications. It demonstrates how dynamic pricing, automated metrics, and algorithmic deactivation erode foundational labor rights, safety, and non-discrimination standards. To bridge this regulatory gap, the chapter proposes an integrated, rights-based governance framework anchored in a statutory rebuttable presumption of employment, algorithmic transparency, co-determination, worker data rights, competition law exemptions for collective bargaining, and portable benefit schemes to secure human dignity in platform capitalism.

title: Neuroderechos y gestión algorítmica en el trabajo: riesgos laborales emergentes y redefinición del deber de prevención del empleador
abstract: This article examines how algorithmic management and neurotechnologies transform occupational risks and the employer’s duty of prevention. Drawing on a legal review of publications from 2015 to 2025 and a doctrinal, functional, and comparative analysis, it examines psychosocial, cognitive, discriminatory, and other risks associated with the processing of neural data. The study compares the safeguards established under European law, International Labour Organization standards, and the Peruvian legal framework governing occupational safety and health, data protection, and artificial intelligence. It identifies difficulties in assessing risks arising from opaque systems, supervising automated decision-making, and safeguarding workers’ right to defend themselves against disciplinary measures. The article proposes clarifying preventive obligations through the provision of clear and comprehensible information, meaningful human involvement in decisions producing significant effects, participatory risk assessments, and limits on the processing of mental data. In the Peruvian context, it distinguishes existing legal obligations from proposed regulatory measures.

title: Leader status-leveling behavior and leadership effectiveness: the roles of warmth-based mechanism and leader gender
abstract: Purpose In response to growing organizational efforts to promote diversity, equity and inclusion, many leaders are encouraged to adopt behaviors that reduce hierarchical distance, known as status-leveling behavior. While prior research has emphasized its benefits for employees, little is known about its effects on leaders themselves. This study aims to shift the focus to examine whether, how and for whom leader status-leveling behavior enhances leadership effectiveness. Design/methodology/approach To investigate these relationships, this study adopted a multi-method approach. This study conducted a video-based scenario experiment (n = 155) and a two-wave field survey (n = 212) to test the proposed theoretical model. Findings The video-based scenario experiment and multi-wave survey results showed that leader status-leveling behavior could promote leadership effectiveness through employee’s perceived leader warmth rather than competence. In addition, the status-leveling behavior of male leaders is more effective than that of female leaders in promoting leadership effectiveness through perceived leader warmth. Originality/value This study advances leadership research by repositioning

title: HireWatch: Evaluating LLM Compliance with U.S. Employment Law Under Contextual Pressure
abstract: The deployment of large language models (LLMs) in hiring pipelines is growing, yet existing evaluations generally overlook their compliance with legal rules. To fill this gap, we introduce HireWatch, an evaluation that assesses whether LLMs comply with U.S. laws that govern the questions that job candidates may be asked. We construct a 200-item bank of lawful and unlawful interview questions, whose legal classification is based on U.S. federal statutes, regulations, and agency guidance. We instruct LLMs to select questions from this bank in preparing for job interviews, across a set of various occupations and contexts, and report the fraction of unlawful questions that LLMs select. Evaluation of 18 closed and open-weight LLMs across ~100,000 trials under different types of contextual pressure reveals that LLMs' legal compliance is brittle. While LLMs generally avoid selecting unlawful questions in low-pressure contexts, legal violations increase sharply under higher pressure. Explicit prompts to comply with law can improve compliance rates, but do not altogether eliminate legal violations. We publicly release our code and data at https://github.com/hnghiem-nlp/hirewatch_repo.

title: Is Algorithmic Control a Double-Edged Sword? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Perceived Algorithmic Control and Platform Workers' Well-being and Work Attitudes
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesizes quantitative studies on the association between platform gig workers' perceived algorithmic control (or algorithmic management) and their well-being, work attitudes, and work behaviors. It estimates overall associations, tests whether distinct dimensions of algorithmic control (e.g., standardized guidance, tracking evaluation, behavioral constraint) relate to outcomes in different directions, and examines contextual and methodological moderators. English-language and Chinese-language literature will be included.

title: AI-Induced Social Erosion: Using LLMs for Work Tasks Reduces Help-Seeking Intentions Towards Colleagues
abstract: Generative AI is becoming embedded in knowledge work as an intelligent collaborator to assist in completing tasks. However, this readily available assistance risks displacing key interactions through which colleague relationships are built and sustained at work. This paper leverages the concept of help-seeking behaviour to investigate whether and how AI usage shapes colleague relationships. We conducted an online experimental vignette study where 248 knowledge workers evaluated scenarios that systematically varied whether and how AI was used across different work tasks. Using linear mixed-effects models, we found that AI-enabled work reduced help-seeking intentions compared to non-AI work across tasks, and especially for brainstorming. Visible AI usage was associated with greater help-seeking intentions towards colleagues, and individual contributors' colleague relationships were more vulnerable than managers. Our findings identify opportunities for workplace AI tools, practices, and policies to preserve colleague relationships in increasingly AI-integrated workplaces.

title: How artificial intelligence shapes employer branding: a systematic review of perceptions and paradoxes
abstract: Purpose This study systematically synthesizes the emerging literature at the intersection of artificial intelligence (AI) and employer branding, addresses fragmentation across concepts, theories and methods and identifies key mechanisms shaping employer-brand-related perceptions and outcomes. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review (SLR) followed PRISMA guidelines, applied the theory–context–methodology (TCM) framework and combined descriptive analysis with thematic synthesis of 21 peer-reviewed studies retrieved from Scopus and Web of Science. Findings AI functions as a socio-technical signal that shapes employer-brand-related perceptions and outcomes through perception-based mechanisms. Organizational attractiveness, application intentions and engagement outcomes are shaped by candidates' perceptions of fairness, trust and emotional responses. A key paradox emerges: AI signals innovation and efficiency, enhancing attractiveness, but may also signal reduced human orientation and cost-driven motives, weakening outcomes. These effects vary by recruitment stage, culture and industry. Research limitations/implications The review is constrained by the relatively smal

title: Algorithmic Bias and Discrimination in Organizational Decision-Making
abstract: As digital transformation increases organizational complexity, many organizations are adopting AI algorithms for critical administrative tasks like recruitment and resource allocation. AI algorithms are sequences of mathematical models that make predictions and provide automated decisions based on datasets. AI algorithms can take decisions on complex problems by using human reasoning and mimicking human cognitive processes. These algorithms are no longer merely tools; they now function as digital agents that manage processes by making autonomous decisions. Therefore, the chapter firstly addresses AI algorithms in organizational decision-making and then clarifies the issues of algorithmic bias and discrimination arising from AI algorithms. Secondly, this study highlights the need for governance mechanisms that align technical systems with organizational authorities' values and legal obligations to help reduce discrimination and bias . Finally, this chapter emphasizes the importance of transparent, ethical, responsible, and inclusive algorithms.

title: GESTÃO DE PESSOAS E IA GENERATIVA: REQUALIFICAÇÃO, SUBSTITUIÇÃO DE FUNÇÕES E EFEITOS SOBRE O CLIMA ORGANIZACIONAL
abstract: A IA generativa entrou nas organizações como ferramenta de produtividade, mas chega aos trabalhadores como decisão sobre o seu trabalho, e a gestão de pessoas responde a ela com duas estratégias principais: requalificar os trabalhadores cujos papéis mudam ou substituir as funções que a tecnologia passa a executar. O artigo pergunta como a gestão de pessoas tem tratado essa adoção e que efeitos cada estratégia tende a produzir sobre o clima organizacional. A análise, uma revisão integrativa de estudos empíricos e teóricos, compara os achados sobre requalificação e deslocamento com as dimensões em que o clima é medido. A requalificação aparece associada a confiança, informação, disposição para adotar a tecnologia e permanência, desde que conduzida com transparência sobre a evolução dos papéis, segurança para experimentar, mentoria e gestores preparados. A substituição atinge quem é dispensado, com perda de identidade e percepção de traição organizacional, atinge quem permanece, pela ansiedade que reduz a adoção, e atinge quem entraria na carreira, pela supressão das tarefas de formação. Na dimensão da igualdade, as duas estratégias concentram ganhos e perdas em grupos diferentes, por

title: Being(s) there(s)—geographies of tacit knowledge through avatars, telepresence robots, and holograms
abstract: We aim to understand emerging geographies of tacit knowledge through advanced remote-work technologies: telepresence robots, holograms and virtual avatars. These technologies enable ‘being there’ in more than one location (and space) at once and using communication that resembles a face-to-face experience. We examine, if tacit knowledge can be shared through these technologies. Based on interviews and autoethnography, we find that each technology confers the ability to exert specific spatial agency elsewhere. From the intellectualist perspective, all studied technologies allow the sharing of some tacit knowledge, whereas virtual avatars enable the sharing of some tacit knowledge also from the phenomenological perspective.

title: Digitalisation de la fonction RH, cognition, bien-être au travail et performance organisationnelle: revue systématique multi-bases et cadre intégrateur à double voie
venue: International Journal of Accounting, Finance, Auditing, Management and Economics
abstract: Objectif : expliquer pourquoi la digitalisation des ressources humaines (RH) est associée à des bénéfices organisationnels et à des contraintes psychosociales parfois simultanées. La fragmentation des synthèses sur l’e-HRM, le technostress et la gestion algorithmique justifie une analyse intégrée des mécanismes d’appropriation. Méthode : revue systématique à visée intégrative de publications de 2007 à 2026, recherches clôturées le 8 septembre 2026 dans Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, Business Source Complete et PsycINFO. Cinquante-deux contributions ont atteint l’étape d’éligibilité , 39 ont été retenues et 13 exclues. La synthèse est narrative, structurée par mécanismes, aucun protocole n’a été préenregistré. Résultats : 27 publications datent de 2022 à 2026, l’audit descriptif initial distingue 24 études de crédibilité élevée et 15 de crédibilité modérée. La voie des ressources associe qualité, utilité, appropriation et autonomie. La voie des demandes associe complexité, surveillance, charge cognitive et technostress. Six travaux sur les technologies numériques générales servent d’appui conceptuel à cette seconde voie, sans valoir preuve directe en contexte RH. Contributi

title: ESTRATÉGIAS DE GESTÃO DE PESSOAS PARA A INCLUSÃO DE PROFISSIONAIS NEURODIVERGENTES NO MERCADO DE TRABALHO BRASILEIRO
abstract: A inclusão de profissionais neurodivergentes no mercado de trabalho ainda apresenta desafios relacionados aos processos de recrutamento e seleção, às condições do ambiente organizacional e à permanência e ao desenvolvimento desses profissionais. O estudo analisa e organiza estratégias de Gestão de Pessoas que podem contribuir para a inclusão de profissionais neurodivergentes, com foco em pessoas com Transtorno do Espectro Autista (TEA) e Transtorno de Déficit de Atenção e Hiperatividade (TDAH). A pesquisa possui abordagem qualitativa e caráter descritivo, desenvolvida por meio de revisão bibliográfica narrativa. Como recurso de análise, utiliza-se uma adaptação teórica do método Quality Function Deployment (QFD), aplicada às necessidades identificadas na literatura, sem realização de pesquisa de campo. A análise organiza as principais demandas relacionadas à inclusão e destaca três eixos recorrentes: treinamento de gestores e equipes de Recursos Humanos, reformulação dos processos seletivos e adaptação dos ambientes físicos e das condições de trabalho. Os resultados indicam que a inclusão efetiva depende não apenas do cumprimento das exigências legais, mas também da adoção de práti

title: QUALIDADE DE VIDA NO TRABALHO EM UMA ORGANIZAÇÃO DE MANAUS: PERCEPÇÕES DOS TRABALHADORES SOBRE CONDIÇÕES, BENEFÍCIOS E DESAFIOS
abstract: Este estudo analisou a percepção de 85 trabalhadores de uma organização localizada no bairro Tarumã, em Manaus, Amazonas, sobre a qualidade de vida no trabalho (QVT), seus benefícios e desafios. A pesquisa é aplicada, quantitativa e descritiva, com levantamento bibliográfico e coleta de dados por formulário eletrônico. A amostra foi não probabilística, formada por adesão voluntária. O instrumento reuniu quatro questões de caracterização e oito sobre QVT. As respostas foram analisadas por frequências e percentuais. As relações interpessoais e as condições de trabalho apresentaram avaliações mais favoráveis, enquanto reconhecimento, desenvolvimento profissional e equilíbrio entre vida profissional e pessoal concentraram proporções maiores de respostas intermediárias ou desfavoráveis. O ambiente saudável (25,9%) e a flexibilidade de horários (23,5%) foram os benefícios mais citados; estresse e pressão (27,1%) e excesso de trabalho (24,7%) foram os desafios mais apontados. Os resultados mostram que avaliações positivas das relações profissionais coexistem com dificuldades de valorização e conciliação entre trabalho e vida pessoal. A contribuição do estudo consiste em identificar essas

title: ATRAÇÃO E SELEÇÃO DE COORDENADORES EM ENSINO SUPERIOR PRIVADO
abstract: O presente artigo analisou os processos de atração e seleção de coordenadores de curso em quatro instituições privadas de ensino superior localizadas na grande Vitória, Espírito Santo, considerando a importância do cargo para a gestão acadêmica. O objetivo foi compreender como essas instituições estruturam suas práticas e identificar os principais desafios enfrentados. A pesquisa é aplicada, descritiva e qualitativa, com coleta de dados por meio de questionário estruturado aplicado a coordenadores de curso. Os resultados mostraram que duas instituições utilizam indicações internas sem divulgação formal, enquanto as demais recorrem a canais digitais como site institucional e redes sociais. Os critérios mais valorizados são experiência na docência, liderança e capacidade de inovação, embora metade das instituições não realize avaliação formal do alinhamento à cultura organizacional. Entre os desafios, destacam-se a baixa atratividade do cargo, a sobrecarga de responsabilidades, a remuneração limitada e a necessidade de que a vaga reflita a complexidade real da função para atender às expectativas dos candidatos e elevar o interesse pela posição. Conclui-se que há necessidade de maior

title: Worker Power, Algorithmic Management, and African Resistance in the Digital Age
The relationship between language ideologies and workplace mistreatment towards North Korean defectors
venue: The International Journal of Human Resource Management
abstract: Previous studies on Social Identity Theory (SIT) have revealed the role of social categorisation in power imbalances between languages, linking it to negative acts in workplaces (e.g. discrimination). We focus on subtle social categorisation along the linguistic dimension, investigating whether North Korean Defectors (NKDs) working at South Korean organisations perceive workplace mistreatment as a result of linguistic discrimination. Repeat interviews were conducted with 20 NKDs, and one-off interviews with 6 NKDs. Our study shows that the use of North Korean accents or lexical items has been regarded as illegitimate in South Korean workplaces, leading NKDs to feel mistreated. We also investigate NKDs’ identity formation in response to workplace mistreatment. Our results show that the majority of NKDs hide their North Korean ethnicity in the workplace for fear of being mistreated due to ingrained stereotypes about NKDs.

title: Why Time Management Leads to Well-Being (and Performance)
abstract: Time management is usually seen as a way to get more done. Yet research suggests that it is more strongly associated with well-being than with performance. Why time management improves well-being and why the benefits vary remain unclear. This article proposes three pathways linking time management to well-being and productivity. First, structure brings order to daily life by giving people a sense of control and predictability. Second, synchrony aligns activities with social and biological rhythms, reducing conflict and strengthening social ties. And third, concordance aligns activities with personal values and long-term goals, giving daily life meaning and strengthening the connection between present and future selves. These benefits depend on both individual practices and organizational conditions. Fragmented work, excessive demands on people’s time, and a focus on short-term results can obstruct the pathways. An imbalance among the pathways can also turn otherwise useful time management practices into sources of strain. By distinguishing these mechanisms and their limits, the framework helps explain why time management can improve well-being and productivity in some circumstances

title: Beyond Green Rhetoric: How Human Resource Management Bridges Strategy and Sustainability in Hotels
abstract: Drawing on the natural resource‐based view (NRBV) and social cognitive theory (SCT), this study examines the relationships among strategic green intentions, green human resource management (Green HRM) practices, sustainable business performance and employee outcomes in Ghana's hospitality industry. Two independent quantitative studies were conducted in star‐rated hotels. Study 1 surveyed 282 managers and supervisors to examine Green HRM practices as mediating mechanisms linking strategic green intentions to economic, social and environmental performance. Study 2 surveyed 302 frontline employees to investigate employee green commitment as a mediator of the relationships between Green HRM practices and employee green behaviour and turnover intention. Data were analysed using a disjoint two‐stage PLS‐SEM approach. Study 1 revealed that strategic green intentions were directly associated with social performance but not with economic or environmental performance. Green HRM practices exhibited significant positive indirect effects across all three performance dimensions, with indirect‐only mediation for economic and environmental performance and complementary mediation for social perform

title: SmartCareer an AI-powered integrated career development and recruitment intelligence platform
abstract: Manual resume screening and single-purpose recruitment tools leave a persistent gap: no existing platform combines candidate-facing career support with recruiter-facing evaluation tools while keeping the scoring process transparent and auditable. This paper presents SmartCareer, an integrated AI-powered career intelligence platform that unifies eight candidate- and recruiter-facing modules—domain-aware resume analysis, skill prediction, applicant tracking system (ATS) scoring, resume enhancement, course/certification recommendation, a voice-enabled mock interview simulator, and recruiter-side resume–job matching with shortlist lifecycle tracking—within a single integrated system. Unlike prior work, which typically addresses one stage of the hiring pipeline in isolation, SmartCareer links resume analysis directly to interview preparation by generating interview questions from the candidate’s own resume and domain profile, and it replaces opaque, black-box matching scores with an interpretable, weighted multi-factor composite score that both candidates and recruiters can inspect component by component. The platform is built as a React.js single-page application with a Flask RESTful b

title: Urban Agglomeration Development Policies and Firms’ Labor Outsourcing: Evidence from China
abstract: Using panel data on Chinese A-share listed firms from 2012 to 2024, this study examines how national urban agglomeration development policies affect labor outsourcing through a staggered difference-in-differences design. Policy implementation significantly increases labor outsourcing intensity, and the finding is robust to alternative estimators and specifications. The mechanism analysis shows that policy implementation is associated with greater firm specialization, increased labor dispute litigation, and lower regional labor market segmentation. The outsourcing response is concentrated in core cities. Further analysis finds lower internal employment and internal labor costs relative to revenue, alongside higher average employee compensation. These findings extend the evaluation of regional integration policies to firms’ organization of labor inputs and highlight the need to distinguish changes in internal employment from changes in firms’ reliance on external labor services.

title: Stakeholder Governance
abstract: Stakeholder governance has become central to debates about stakeholder capitalism, yet research remains fragmented about the configurations through which non-shareholder stakeholders gain authority and firms become credibly bound to stakeholder claims. We systematically review 171 articles in management and related fields to develop a framework organized around stakeholder authority (i.e., the participatory rights or recognized standing through which stakeholders can engage in governance), and firm commitment (i.e., the obligations organizations assume toward stakeholder claims in ways that are costly to reverse or ignore). We identify five recurring configurations: (a) disclosure and evaluation; (b) monitoring and verification; (c) contracting, formal rules, and adjudication; (d) governance rights; and (e) rule-making rights. These configurations generally move from informational authority and very weak firm commitment to constitutional authority and very strong firm commitment. We also identify two off-diagonal configurations—constrained authority and embedded commitment—that reveal how authority and commitment need not align. title: Digital CSR communication and sustainable talent management discourses on Facebook and YouTube: a computational analysis from Jordan
abstract: This study examines how corporate social responsibility (CSR) and sustainable talent management themes are represented and received in public Facebook and YouTube interactions in Jordan. The analysis draws on 34,150 anonymized digital-trace records collected between 1 January and 30 June 2025, comprising 18,430 Facebook interactions and 15,720 YouTube interactions. A computational content analysis design integrates topic-model-derived labels, sentiment scoring, engagement metrics, and a descriptive centrality indicator. Five substantive topics were represented in the corpus, led by sustainable work practices (28.1%) and youth empowerment (22.1%). Sentiment was predominantly positive on both platforms, but the platform difference in categorical sentiment was not statistically significant, χ 2 (2, N = 34,097) = 4.44, p = 0.109, Cramér's V = 0.011. Mean sentiment polarity likewise did not differ significantly between Facebook and YouTube, t (34,148) = 1.45, p = 0.147, d = 0.016. Total engagement was also statistically similar across platforms and content formats. These findings qualify stronger platform-difference claims and suggest that, within this corpus, substantive CSR and talent

title: DESAFIO DA RETENÇÃO DE TALENTOS EM MICROEMPRESAS BRASILEIRAS: FATORES ORGANIZACIONAIS, FINANCEIROS E DE GESTÃO
abstract: As microempresas ocupam posição central na economia brasileira, mas enfrentam dificuldades persistentes para reter profissionais qualificados, em um mercado de trabalho que registrou 9,2 milhões de desligamentos a pedido em 2025. Este artigo tem como objetivo analisar quais fatores organizacionais, financeiros e de gestão influenciam a retenção de talentos em microempresas brasileiras, a fim de identificar estratégias eficazes para reduzir a rotatividade e ampliar a permanência dos colaboradores. Trata-se de pesquisa aplicada, de abordagem qualitativa e caráter exploratório e descritivo, desenvolvida por meio de revisão bibliográfica narrativa, complementada por dados secundários de fontes oficiais e institucionais. O levantamento abrangeu Google Acadêmico, Portal de Periódicos da CAPES, SciELO, SPELL, BDTD e repositórios institucionais, com publicações de 2015 a 2026, e o material foi examinado por meio da análise de conteúdo de Bardin. Os resultados indicam que a retenção é multifatorial: liderança, clima organizacional, comunicação, reconhecimento e desenvolvimento pesam tanto quanto a remuneração, cuja eficácia depende da percepção de justiça. title: Generative artificial intelligence in human resource management: a bibliometric analysis and research agenda
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), epitomised by large language models such as ChatGPT, is rapidly reshaping human resource management (HRM), yet research at this intersection remains fragmented across management, information systems and computer science. This study maps the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of the emerging GenAI-HRM field and proposes an agenda for future inquiry. Following the PRISMA 2020 protocol, 340 peer-reviewed articles and reviews published between 2023 and July 2026 were retrieved from the Scopus database and analysed through bibliometric performance analysis and science mapping, combining keyword co-occurrence, country co-authorship, bibliographic coupling, thematic mapping based on centrality and density, and trend-topic analysis. The results show that the field is young but expanding exponentially, growing from 8 documents in 2023 to 137 in the first seven months of 2026 and accumulating 4,803 citations, with output led by the United States, China, India and the United Kingdom and dispersed across management, information systems and applied computing outlets. Four thematic clusters emerge: AI-enabled recruitment and talent acquisiti

title: Procedural Provisions of the Pay Transparency Directive: A Procedural (R)evolution?
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The EU Pay Transparency Directive has already generated considerable discussion. Some of its procedural provisions have also attracted criticism. This presentation examines a selection of these procedural provisions, analyses their impact on Belgian law, and assesses whether those concerns are well-founded.

title: Artificial Intelligence, Gender Bias, and Human Rights: Challenges for Modern Justice Systems
venue: Interdisciplinary Journal of Research and Development
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become increasingly integrated into modern justice systems, influencing decision-making in criminal justice, hiring, surveillance, healthcare, and public administration. Although AI promises efficiency and consistency, a growing body of research documents risks of algorithmic bias and unequal performance across demographic groups. This paper examines the relationship between artificial intelligence, gender bias, and human rights within contemporary justice systems through a qualitative, interdisciplinary analysis combining a narrative review of scholarly literature with doctrinal analysis of relevant international and European legal and ethical frameworks. It considers how biased datasets, discriminatory or uneven algorithmic outcomes, and unequal technological representation may affect fairness, equality, privacy, due process, and access to justice. Particular attention is given to documented evidence on facial-analysis systems and automated recruitment, while broader claims concerning institutional legitimacy and human-centered justice are treated as normative implications rather than empirical findings. The paper also evaluates regulatory respons

title: Sustainable HRM for Organizational Performance and Sustainable Development: The Moderating Role of Analytics
abstract: Sustainable HRM and the associated concepts such as Green HRM and Social HRM, are gaining much prominence in contemporary strategic as well as scholarly discussions owing to their association with organizational performance. Owing to the various socio-economic and environmental challenges, organizations worldwide are expected to align their strategies and practices towards the accomplishment of the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Data analytics implementation too, is garnering both business and research interest owing to its positive contribution to organizational performance. This paper aims to propose a model connecting all these concepts. Based on an extensive yet focused review of literature, the authors have designed a conceptual model explaining the relationship among sustainable HRM, HR analytics application, organizational performance, and sustainable development. It may be concluded that organizations can boost their performance by implementing sustainable HRM principles and practices while contributing to SDGs. This research also affirms the influence of HR analytics as a moderating variable in the relationship between the comprehensively defined sus

title: AI Deactivation Reduces Loneliness and Increases Social Interaction
abstract: General-purpose artificial intelligence (AI) assistants are increasingly embedded in everyday life, transforming how people accomplish tasks and potentially reshaping how they interact with others. Prior research has focused on how using AI for explicitly social purposes affects users' psychological well-being and social lives. Yet such uses account for only a small portion of interactions with general-purpose AI assistants. Whether using AI for everyday, instrumental tasks affects users' psychological well-being and social behavior remains unclear. Here we investigate these effects through a longitudinal deactivation experiment with active ChatGPT users (N=625), in which participants were randomly assigned to abstain from using AI assistants for either fourteen days (treatment) or one day (control). Participants used AI predominantly for instrumental purposes, with 84.7% reporting productivity as their most frequent use case. Two weeks of deactivation significantly reduced loneliness relative to the control group ($β= -0.10$, $p=0.03$), with reductions persisting two weeks after participants resumed using AI ($β= -0.16$, $p=0.02$). title: Navigating Global Paradoxes: International Business Strategy and the Corporate DEI Exodus
venue: Journal of Teaching in International Business
abstract: This case examines the strategic and ethical challenges businesses face when pursuing corporate social responsibility (CSR), particularly diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI), initiatives across fragmented global markets. Divergent political, social, and economic pressures often conflict sharply with financial performance objectives. Despite CSR’s mainstream status, the tension between profitability and social obligations remains under-addressed, especially in international management literature. This tension intensified significantly following the 2024 U.S. presidential election, triggering a widespread corporate retreat from DEI programs. Using a composite multinational firm (AuroraTech Inc.) grounded in empirical data from 2020–2025, the case places students in the role of CEO Maya Cooper. She must navigate declining revenues, activist investor pressure, employee attrition, and conflicting cross-border stakeholder expectations. Students are challenged to evaluate financial and non-financial metrics, assess the validity of ROI attributions for CSR investments, manage regional institutional differences, and determine how the company can uphold its core values (“Technology with P

title: BURNOUT COMO INDICADOR DE GESTÃO: CUSTOS ORGANIZACIONAIS DO ADOECIMENTO MENTAL E A EFICÁCIA DE POLÍTICAS DE JORNADA REDUZIDA
abstract: O esgotamento profissional deixa marcas dispersas nas organizações: atestados, faltas, demissões, horas acumuladas e queda de desempenho, registrados em lugares diferentes e raramente lidos em conjunto. Ao mesmo tempo, a redução da jornada aparece como resposta ao adoecimento mental. O artigo pergunta em que medida o burnout serve como indicador de gestão nas organizações brasileiras, considerando os custos de afastamento, absenteísmo, rotatividade e perda de produtividade, e o que a evidência permite afirmar sobre a eficácia da jornada reduzida para diminuir esses custos. A análise se apoia em estudos sobre burnout e afastamentos e na legislação federal sobre jornada e saúde do trabalhador. Os resultados mostram que há instrumentos validados para medir a síndrome no Brasil e que a lei já obriga a produzir a maior parte dos registros de custo, mas cada registro capta só parte do problema: os dados previdenciários diluem a síndrome em diagnósticos vizinhos, a rotatividade nem sempre acompanha o esgotamento e as horas registradas dependem do controle exercido. O burnout funciona como indicador quando composto pela medida periódica da exaustão emocional e pelos registros de custo, lid

title: O USO DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL EM RECRUTAMENTO E SELEÇÃO: IMPACTOS NA PRODUTIVIDADE DO RH E NA PERCEPÇÃO DE JUSTIÇA DOS CANDIDATOS
abstract: Este artigo analisa o que a literatura científica publicada entre 2021 e 2026 permite afirmar sobre os efeitos do uso da inteligência artificial (IA) no recrutamento e seleção sobre a produtividade do setor de recursos humanos e o que ela permite inferir sobre a justiça dos processos seletivos e a experiência dos candidatos. Realizou-se uma revisão bibliográfica integrativa nas bases SciELO e SPELL, com descritores em português, inglês e espanhol. Dos 74 registros identificados, 17 eram duplicados e 42 foram excluídos na leitura de títulos e resumos, resultando em 15 estudos: sete primários, cinco secundários e três análises jurídico-normativas, avaliados quanto à qualidade metodológica e examinados por Análise de Conteúdo. Os resultados indicam que os ganhos de produtividade são relatados por gestores, recrutadores e fornecedores, sobretudo na triagem de currículos, mas nenhum estudo primário os mensurou com indicadores objetivos. Quanto à justiça, nenhum estudo investigou diretamente os candidatos; as evidências disponíveis, provenientes de profissionais de RH, decisores e análises normativas, apontam riscos de viés algorítmico, baixa transparência e redução do contato humano, al

title: Generative AI collaboration and expatriate career adaptability: a career construction perspective on sustainable career development
venue: The International Journal of Human Resource Management
abstract: As generative AI (GenAI) technologies become increasingly integrated into global workplaces, their implications for individual career development, particularly among internationally mobile professionals, remain underexplored. This study examines the relationship between human–GenAI collaboration and expatriates’ career adaptability, as well as three career sustainability-related outcomes: career satisfaction, life satisfaction, and perceived AI-enabled task performance. Grounded in Career Construction Theory, the study conceptualizes human–GenAI collaboration as a contextual resource associated with adaptive career responses. Drawing on data from 361 expatriates, the findings indicate that human–GenAI collaboration is positively associated with career adaptability, which in turn relates positively to these career-related outcomes. The results further show that the relationship between human–GenAI collaboration and career adaptability varies according to expatriates’ AI trust and perceived AI-induced job insecurity. This study contributes to research on career development and human–AI interaction by highlighting the role of digitally mediated work practices in adaptive career proces

title: Cognitive Ambidexterity: Balancing Algorithmic Efficiency and Contextual Judgement in AI-Enabled Decision Systems
abstract: AI-enabled decision systems make algorithmic recommendations appear objective and ready for action before contextual, ethical, and stakeholder concerns are fully considered. This study examines how leaders preserve judgment under these conditions. We develop cognitive ambidexterity as a leader-level meta-cognitive capability through which managers balance algorithmic exploitation with contextual exploration in AI-mediated decisions. Using an exploratory sequential mixed-methods design, we first examine five U.K. procurement and infrastructure organizations and identify four mechanisms of cognitive ambidexterity. We then examine these mechanisms through vignette experiments with managers. The findings show that leaders preserve contextual judgment by treating AI outputs as interpretive cues, calibrating trust under ambiguity, slowing decisions when reflection is needed, and building supports that make algorithmic recommendations contestable. The study extends ambidexterity theory by showing how exploration–exploitation tensions are cognitively regulated when exploitation is embedded in algorithmic decision processes. It also uses leadership cognition and Upper Echelons Theory to exp

title: Explainable AI for Fair and Transparent Human Resource Decision- Making
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Human resource (HR) decisions are currently supported by algorithmic processes for hiring, promotions, and retaining employees, the lack of transparency in these models raises concerns about fairness, accountability, and trust of employees towards the process. In this paper, we develop a two-channel explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) model that combines the post hoc explanation methods such as SHAP and LIME with the inherently interpretable classifier for HR decisions. In our methodology, adversarial debiasing is used in the training process to prevent the influence of sensitive attributes on the model performance. For testing the effectiveness of the proposed XAI model, we conduct an experimental evaluation using IBM HR analytics dataset with three HR decision making tasks including promotion prediction, attrition prediction, and candidate selection task. As results, we show that our model achieves reductions in demographic parity disparity without compromising the explanation quality using local accuracy and stability measures. Comparing with baseline models in terms of fairness-utility trade-off consistently yields improvements.

title: From Organisational Trust to AI Adoption: Examining the Role of Perceived Fairness, Transparency, and Employee Confidence in AI-Enabled Human Resource Management
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming human resource management (HRM) through its applications in recruitment and selection, performance evaluation, employee engagement, learning and development, workforce planning, and talent management. Despite the operational benefits of AI-enabled HRM, employee acceptance remains influenced by concerns regarding algorithmic fairness, transparency, accountability, privacy, and the reliability of automated decisions. This study develops and examines a framework explaining how perceived fairness, transparency, and employee confidence contribute to organisational trust and how organisational trust subsequently influences employees’ intention to adopt AI-enabled HRM systems. The study is conceptually grounded in organisational trust theory, organisational justice theory, and technology acceptance perspectives. A quantitative, cross-sectional research design is proposed, with an sample of 160 employees and HR professionals working in Indian organisations. A structured questionnaire based on a five-point Likert scale is used as the proposed measurement instrument. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, construct validity ass

title: The Predictive Influence of Management Leadership Styles on Employee Retention: A Quantitative Study in the Aerospace and Defense Industry
abstract: The Aerospace and Defense (A&D) industry in Northern Virginia faces a critical talent shortage exacerbated by high employee turnover and a retiring workforce. Replacing professionals holding specialized security clearances is commonly estimated at 150 to 250 percent of their annual salary. This quantitative, non-experimental applied research examined the predictive relationship between management leadership style and employee turnover intent within this sector. Grounded in Fiedler's Contingency Theory and Leader-Member Exchange Theory, the study surveyed 773 professionals across seven major organizations to measure turnover intent, management leadership style, job satisfaction, and leader support. Hierarchical multiple regression isolated leadership style's association with turnover intent from four demographic controls: age, gender, role, and years of service. The results showed that demographic variables accounted for 7.5 percent of the variance in turnover intent, and a composite leadership-style score explained an additional, independent 14.8 percent. title: Preparing Europe’s Transport Workforce for CCAM – The RESKILLING Employment and Skills Observatory
abstract: In the face of persistent challenges—including the energy crisis, supply chain disruptions, and rising living costs— the EU labour market remains resilient, with employment reaching a record 213.7 million. Within this context, the transport sector, which contributes 5% to the EU’s GDP and accounts for 3.1% of total employment, is experiencing significant transformation through the adoption of Cooperative, Connected, and Automated Mobility (CCAM) technologies. While CCAM presents opportunities for innovation, economic growth, and job creation, it also poses risks of workforce displacement and evolving skill demands. Addressing these shifts requires a systemic approach that considers not only transport-specific roles but also broader impacts across the value chain, including education, organisational transformation, and labour market dynamics. Ensuring inclusive transitions, reskilling opportunities, and the attractiveness of transport careers is essential. To this extent, the Horizon Europe project RESKILLING (G101147328) introduces the CCAM Employment & Skills Observatory, an AI-powered tool designed to identify and map evolving skill needs, detect emerging roles, and generate tail

title: Employment opportunities and discrimination faced by individuals with mental illness
abstract: Background: This study examines the employment experiences of peer workers with lived experience of mental illness in the Czech Republic, focusing on access to the open labour market, employment duration, and workplace discrimination. The aim was to analyse employment trajectories before and during peer work and to explore relationships between employment outcomes, discrimination, and selected sociodemographic characteristics. Methods: A quantitative survey was conducted among peer workers in health and social services (N = 101). Data were analysed using descriptive statistics, analysis of variance (ANOVA), and chi-square tests. Results: A proportion of respondents reported experiencing discrimination during their job search and in the workplace, including rejection in recruitment, negative interactions with colleagues, and exclusion by supervisors. Most respondents reported a strong interest in employment; however, many described employment trajectories that did not correspond to their qualifications. A statistically significant association with a large effect size was found between employment duration and job position. A significant association was also found between employment d

title: Supply Chain Talent in the Digital Era
abstract: Talent shortages are constraining digital transformation in logistics and supply chain management (LSCM). This mixed-methods study combines a survey of 179 professionals across 21 countries (Africa-led sample), five expert interviews, and an embedded case from Kaduna State, Nigeria. Respondents view AI/ML (≈60.9%), data analytics (≈49.2%), and IoT (≈45.3%) as most impactful, yet ≈61.5% report no emerging-technology training in the past two years. Top barriers are cost (≈72.6%), limited organizational support (≈40.2%), and access to relevant programs (≈30.1%); preferred formats are blended, work-embedded approaches (≈60.3%). Professional development and career growth consistently outrank compensation as retention levers. The case evidence indicates that project-based learning with real tools/datasets, co-designed with academic/industry partners, accelerates adoption and mobility but should be generalized cautiously. We propose a practical KPI set—time-to-productivity, tech-adoption lead time, internal mobility, role-specific retention, and learning gain—to monitor impact. The findings offer actionable guidance for building a future-ready LSCM workforce.

title: The Illusion of Flexibility: Work-Life Balance and Time Control Among Gig Employees
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The proliferation of digital platform labor across urban India has been largely driven by the promise of schedule autonomy and temporal freedom. However, emerging empirical evidence suggests that for many platform workers, this freedom is fundamentally paradoxical. This article examines how algorithmic management, financial precarity, dynamic incentive structures, and market volatility convert promised autonomy into pervasive temporal discipline within the Indian gig landscape. Drawing on a mixed-methods investigation of 450 location-based and web-based gig employees across major metropolitan hubs in India including Bengaluru, Mumbai, and the National Capital Region (NCR), we analyze the structural mechanisms that dictate time control and severely compromise work-life balance. Our findings indicate that while gig employees experience high initial levels of perceived schedule control, their actual temporal flexibility is heavily constrained by dynamic surge pricing algorithms, target-based peak incentives, customer rating penalties, and baseline economic necessity. Consequently, gig employees suffer elevated levels of work-family conflict, unpredictable work schedules, severe physic

title: Technology and the Future of Cross-Cultural Work
abstract: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital collaboration platforms is transforming global employment, transcending geographic and cultural boundaries. This chapter examines how AI-driven systems in hiring, performance evaluation, and management introduce efficiency but also embed cultural biases, creating an “algorithmic glass ceiling.” It highlights the emergence of “Third Digital Cultures” shaped by open-source communities and tech ecosystems, promoting shared global norms. However, the persistent digital divide risks excluding developing regions from these benefits. The chapter concludes by advocating “cultural intelligence by design,” emphasizing inclusive, ethical AI systems that balance technological standardization with cultural diversity to foster an equitable global workforce.

title: Navigating Authenticity and Adversity: A Qualitative Exploration of Employment Experiences of Transgender and Gender Diverse Texans
abstract: Transgender and gender‐diverse (TGD) individuals face elevated rates of employment discrimination, with consequences for economic stability and psychological well‐being. However, three gaps limit current understanding: the institutional mechanisms through which cisnormative workplaces legally and structurally produce exclusion remain undertheorized; job‐seeking as a distinct stage of employment vulnerability is largely unexamined; and no prior qualitative study has investigated TGD employment in a Southern US state during a period of organized legislative hostility toward the population. This study addresses these gaps through a qualitative exploration of TGD employment experiences in Texas—a context where cisnormative exclusion is actively reinforced by the absence of statewide anti‐discrimination protections and by religious exemption litigation under the Religious Freedom Restoration Act, making it theoretically distinct from states that only lack TGD protections. Drawing on Puwar's (2004) Bodies Out of Place (BOP) framework and Turner's (2024) extension to transgender experience, we analyzed data from three focus groups and three individual interviews with 11 TGD Texans, using

title: Cognitive Offloading and Automation Bias in Generative AI-Assisted Learning Systems: A Systematic Review and Secondary Evidence Synthesis
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: The use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools in learning systems is growing rapidly and is changing the way people learn, solve problems and make decisions. Cognitive offloading refers to the transfer of mental tasks such as remembering, reasoning and evaluating to external systems, while automation bias describes the tendency to rely on the output of automated systems in place of independent judgement. Both phenomena are more visible in generative AI settings, because these systems produce fluent, human-like responses that imitate the process of reasoning itself. Over-reliance on generative AI can therefore threaten intellectual independence and accountability for decisions: it tends to reduce verification behaviour, weaken skill development and increase the risk of reasoning errors, particularly in educational and workplace learning. This paper examines the role of cognitive offloading and automation bias in generative AI-supported learning systems through a systematic review and secondary evidence synthesis of recent empirical studies from educational, technical and professional fields. The results show that unstructured use of generative AI is frequently associated

title: Gestão de Pessoas e Adequação de Competências na Execução de Obras e Serviços Técnicos em uma Microempresa
abstract: A obra *Administração & Gestão: Um Olhar para o Futuro Organizacional - Vol. 14* apresenta uma abordagem voltada às discussões contemporâneas no campo da administração e da gestão, considerando perspectivas relacionadas ao futuro das organizações. O material contribui para a reflexão sobre a dinâmica organizacional e os desafios que acompanham as transformações nos ambientes de gestão. Destina-se a estudantes, pesquisadores, docentes e profissionais interessados em ampliar seus conhecimentos sobre administração, práticas organizacionais e perspectivas futuras para a área. %

title: AUTOMAÇÃO E EFICIÊNCIA: IMPACTOS DA INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NA GESTÃO TRABALHISTA E CONTÁBIL
abstract: Este estudo analisou os impactos da Inteligência Artificial (IA) na automação e na eficiência da gestão trabalhista e contábil, considerando os benefícios, os limites e os desafios para o profissional de Ciências Contábeis. Para isso, foi feita uma pesquisa bibliográfica, de abordagem qualitativa e caráter exploratório, com leitura interpretativa e comparação de nove publicações sobre automação de rotinas, folha de pagamento, gestão de pessoas, eficiência operacional e mudanças na profissão contábil. Os resultados mostraram aplicações em lançamentos, conciliações, classificação de documentos, cálculos tributários e trabalhistas, auditoria, relatórios e identificação de inconsistências. Também foram observados ganhos de tempo, melhor organização das informações, aumento da produtividade e redução de falhas manuais. Conclui-se que a IA pode tornar os processos mais ágeis e integrados, mas seus benefícios dependem da qualidade dos dados, da integração dos sistemas, da capacitação e da supervisão humana. A responsabilidade do contador continua, e sua atuação tende a se ampliar para funções analíticas, consultivas e estratégicas.

AI Transforms Healthcare at Providence: Pacesetter Winner
abstract: The healthcare industry is no stranger to challenges around hiring and retaining critical talent. But for Providence , a not-for-profit healthcare system with over 119,000 caregivers, the challenge wasn’t demand—employees wanted to stay and grow. The internal transfer process, however, was getting in the way. In this episode, we speak with Carol McDaniel, Vice President of Talent Acquisition at Providence, a 2026 HR Pacesetter Award winner — about how her team reimagined the internal transfer experience from the ground up, not by patching an existing process, but by rebuilding it entirely through human-centered design. The result is RITA — the Requisition and Internal Transfer Assistant — an AI-powered tool that has not only made transfers seamless—it has also given leaders time back to reinvest in patient care. Carol McDaniel is Vice President of Talent Acquisition at Providence where she focuses on driving hiring innovation, operational effectiveness, and a culture of excellence. She brings more than two decades of experience to her work, with previous roles at Randstad, Delta Airlines, and Johns Hopkins All Children’s Hospital. title: People Analytics and Employee Retention: A Descriptive Study of Data-Driven Approaches to Understanding and Reducing Employee Turnover
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Employee retention is a strategic concern because departures can disrupt operations, weaken institutional knowledge, increase recruitment and training costs, and affect team morale. Traditional practices such as exit interviews, engagement surveys and retrospective turnover reports remain useful but may not identify emerging risks in time. People analytics combines workforce data, statistical analysis and, where appropriate, machine-learning techniques to support better HR decisions. This paper examines the contribution of people analytics to employee retention through a descriptive and conceptual review of the academic literature. It discusses turnover theories, workforce data, analytical methods, HR applications and the ethical conditions required for responsible implementation. It proposes a framework in which data quality and analytical capability support the identification of retention drivers, insights inform fair and targeted interventions, and evaluation supports continuous improvement. title: Responsible AI in human resource management: a sustainable framework for employee trust and organisational performance
venue: Journal of Organizational Effectiveness People and Performance
abstract: Purpose This paper examines how responsible artificial intelligence (AI) governance in human resource management (HRM) may support employee trust and sustainable organisational performance. Design/methodology/approach A conceptual model, developed through purposive theoretical synthesis, connects employee-visible governance with justice, focal trust, employee responses and organisational outcomes, while specifying contextual conditions and learning feedback. Findings The framework proposes that employee-visible responsible AI governance informs justice perceptions, which inform trust in organisationally governed AI-enabled HRM decision processes. Trust may support calibrated reliance and constructive responses; individual performance and collective emergence may then contribute to sustainable organisational performance. Socio-technical alignment, contextual conditions and organisational learning delimit this pathway. The six governance dimensions and twelve propositions are conceptual and have not been empirically validated. title: The implications of digital leadership for productivity, innovation, and employee well-being: a systematic literature review
abstract: Purpose This systematic literature review examines digital leadership as a socio-technical capability that sustains digital transformation. Grounded in the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) model, it examines which employee- and organizational-level outcomes are associated with digital leadership, which mechanisms mediate these relationships, and which contextual factors moderate these effects. Design/methodology/approach Following PRISMA 2020 principles, 47 sources published between 2020 and early 2026 were identified and synthesized, comprising 46 empirical studies and one conceptual-analytical contribution. These 46 empirical studies were appraised for methodological quality using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT). Outcomes were classified along the JD-R model’s motivational and health impairment pathways, and methodological appraisal was adopted to interpret the synthesized evidence. Findings Digital leadership correlates with more innovative work behavior, engagement, empowerment, and well-being; lower technostress; and organizational success in digital transformation, agility, and innovation performance. title: Algorithmic Management and Employee Well-Being: A Text Mining and Behavioral Science Review (2020–2026)
abstract: Algorithmic management (AM)—the use of algorithms and data-driven systems to allocate, monitor, evaluate and discipline work—has expanded from platform labor into conventional organizations and is increasingly linked to employee well-being. This review maps 255 publications from the reference corpus supplied for this study (nominal window 2020–2026) by combining a transparent title-level text-mining workflow, a behavioral-science coding frame and a reference-by-reference narrative synthesis in which every record is discussed. Methods: titles were parsed, tokenized and screened with stop-word removal; term and bigram frequencies, six theme codes and theme co-occurrence were computed, and the records were then synthesized in seventeen thematic sections covering conceptual foundations, platform-worker evidence, double-edged effects, autonomy, technostress, surveillance, fairness, trust, behavioral outcomes, AI adoption, AI-based well-being tools, careers, Industry 5.0 and sectoral contexts. title: On the Challenges of Using LLMs in High-Risk AI Recruitment: Guiding Questions for Legal Conformity with the AI Act
abstract: The EU Artificial Intelligence Act (AI Act) imposes detailed obligations on providers of high-risk AI systems but offers limited operational guidance, particularly when these systems integrate third-party General-Purpose AI (GPAI) models. This paper introduces a toolkit that fosters the development of legal-by-design AI-assisted recruitment systems by translating the core legal obligations of the AI Act's conformity assessment---specifically Articles 9--15 and Annex IV---into techno-normative requirements and corresponding guiding questions. While recruitment pipelines may involve components with varying technical complexity and differing levels of algorithmic transparency, this paper focuses on the most challenging case: the integration of third-party GPAI models into critical stages of the selection process, including resume and job description parsing, applicant scoring, and shortlist generation. This scenario presents significant challenges for downstream providers of high-risk AI systems, as it underscores the difficulties in obtaining the technical information needed to demonstrate compliance with the AI Act's techno-normative requirements, both prior to and during market dep

title: Longing for community: Academics’ dystopian and utopian imaginaries of remote work in the future university
abstract: Purpose In this paper, we explore how academics envision the future university and the role of remote work within it by exploring utopian and dystopian imaginaries, based on 12 in-depth individual interviews with senior academics at a large Norwegian university. We approach imaginaries as a “history of the present”, and draw on Lauren Berlant’s theorization of affect, hope and “cruel optimism” in our interpretation. Major findings Participants’ responses were overwhelmingly dystopian, focused on potential threats to their sense of community and professional identity. Four dystopian scenarios emerged: the Factory, Desert, Anarchy, and Micronation, each highlighting different dimensions of fear, including bureaucratization, dehumanization, atomization, and insulation. The dystopias were often portrayed as already partly unfolding in the present. Alternative hopeful imaginaries were mostly framed as partial and pragmatic acts of resistance, aimed at limiting negative outcomes. Across imaginaries, the longing for community remained a central theme. title: When Climate Incentives Matter: CEO Compensation Design and Stock Market Responses to Climate Transition Risk in Europe
abstract: As climate transition risk becomes increasingly priced in capital markets, firms face growing pressure to demonstrate their preparedness for the low‐carbon transition. Climate‐linked CEO incentives have emerged as a prominent governance mechanism, yet their market relevance remains unclear. Using a sample of listed European firms from 2018 to 2022, we examine when climate‐linked CEO incentives are associated with stock market responses to climate transition shocks. We find that a greater economic weight of climate‐linked compensation is associated with more favorable market responses. This association varies with incentive design and context. Transition‐oriented KPIs exhibit the largest association, whereas process‐oriented KPIs also show a positive association. Broader environmental KPIs, by contrast, show no significant association, although this result may partly reflect their low prevalence in the sample. Moreover, the association is stronger when transition risk is more economically material, emerges under stronger internal climate governance, and is further strengthened by greater responsible capital ownership. title: Reskilling female entrepreneurs for knowledge spillovers: a KSTE perspective on SMEs in lagging regions
abstract: Purpose The research focuses on how territorial innovation aids the process of reskilling and training female entrepreneurs in small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) through knowledge application and spillover in disadvantaged areas. Based on the knowledge spillover theory of entrepreneurship (KSTE), this study aims to investigate the role of institutional help as an essential tool tying together the development of entrepreneurial competence and application of knowledge. Design/methodology/approach The study uses quantitative research techniques based on structural equation modeling that help identify the correlations between obtaining skills by female entrepreneurs and getting managerial training and implementing innovations in their region concerning knowledge gain and usage. Findings The findings show that territorial innovation enhances entrepreneurial capabilities through reskilling and managerial education, while institutional support facilitates the translation of these capabilities into knowledge application and knowledge spillovers.
